# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# This function's decomp project — the PINNED benchmark branch (provenance base + one
# integration commit). Not needed to run this script (inputs are embedded/vendored); to
# rebuild the project itself:
#   git clone --branch asmlift-benchmark https://github.com/macabeus/ac-decomp.git ac-decomp
#   make -C ac-decomp
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH module foresta's symbol map (the module's own symbols over the
# base ELF's globals — this function lives in a REL module, and its code names the module's
# symbols), vendored at apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/symbols/foresta.json.gz
#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: 1c0cf8cc46e28c086cae896eaa8620594f1cbb9b8a2800118f784919e9f2ec31
# Set PROJECT_PATH to your BUILT checkout of the project above (clone recipe in the comments);
# step 1 then points the scoring config at the checkout's decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.elf) —
# the CLI loads the same map, so this run reproduces the row's named spellings. A missing
# checkout/ELF warns and runs map-less (output may then differ from the row).
# Step 3 passes --module foresta: the CLI then reads that module's ELF, which the build writes
# beside the one decomp.yaml names, and places its sections instead of collapsing them onto 0x0.
PROJECT_PATH='/path/to/ac-decomp'

# --project-root grafts the checkout's tools.asmlift.elf (the symbol map) into that decomp.yaml.

pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target ac-decomp:aBALL_actor_move:mwcc_242_81 --out "$PWD" --project-root "$PROJECT_PATH" 1>&2

# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# rebuild the project itself:
#   git clone --branch asmlift-benchmark https://github.com/macabeus/ac-decomp.git ac-decomp

#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: 1c0cf8cc46e28c086cae896eaa8620594f1cbb9b8a2800118f784919e9f2ec31

# step 1 then points the scoring config at the checkout's decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.elf) —
# the CLI loads the same map, so this run reproduces the row's named spellings. A missing
# checkout/ELF warns and runs map-less (output may then differ from the row).
# Step 3 passes --module foresta: the CLI then reads that module's ELF, which the build writes
# beside the one decomp.yaml names, and places its sections instead of collapsing them onto 0x0.
PROJECT_PATH='/path/to/ac-decomp'

# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile

# --project-root grafts the checkout's tools.asmlift.elf (the symbol map) into that decomp.yaml.

# The project declarations the benchmark lifted this row against (asmlift's --context): the row's
# vendored unit context, VERBATIM. What it declares decides spellings, e.g. a member of a struct
# array the project declares is spelled through that array. It is not always the scoring rung
# step 1 writes as ctx.i, which can be smaller.
gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/ctx-323aa9c88f96.i.gz" > declarations.i

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
# (real tier: candidates are scored INSIDE a project context — step 1 materializes ONE rung of
# the benchmark's escalation ladder next to target.o as ctx.i, and the generated decomp.yaml
# concatenates it ahead of every candidate. That rung is the one THIS ROW'S PUBLISHED SOURCE
# stops at — the richest rung on a row asmlift declined — while the harness escalates PER
# CANDIDATE. So this reproduces the row; it does not reproduce a CHANGED asmlift, whose new
# candidate may name a project type this rung does not declare. See docs/ranked-repro.md,
# "What this vehicle does NOT reproduce".)
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target mwcc_242_81    # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name aINS_destruct    # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --asm-data dump.txt     # the data sections above (jump-table/const recovery)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --context declarations.i # the project declarations above
  --module foresta        # the REL module this function lives in: its ELF is the row's symbol map
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

# vendored unit context, VERBATIM. What it declares decides spellings, e.g. a member of a struct
# array the project declares is spelled through that array. It is not always the scoring rung
# step 1 writes as ctx.i, which can be smaller.
gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/ctx-e2905acd8eed.i.gz" > declarations.i

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
# (real tier: candidates are scored INSIDE a project context — step 1 materializes ONE rung of
# the benchmark's escalation ladder next to target.o as ctx.i, and the generated decomp.yaml
# concatenates it ahead of every candidate. That rung is the one THIS ROW'S PUBLISHED SOURCE
# stops at — the richest rung on a row asmlift declined — while the harness escalates PER
# CANDIDATE. So this reproduces the row; it does not reproduce a CHANGED asmlift, whose new
# candidate may name a project type this rung does not declare. See docs/ranked-repro.md,
# "What this vehicle does NOT reproduce".)
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target mwcc_242_81    # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name aINS_get_catch_range_sub # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --asm-data dump.txt     # the data sections above (jump-table/const recovery)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --context declarations.i # the project declarations above
  --module foresta        # the REL module this function lives in: its ELF is the row's symbol map
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

# Reproduce m2c on `aNGD_check_talk_msg_no` — benchmark function ac-decomp:aNGD_check_talk_msg_no:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'
# asmlift checkout — this function's context is the project's own vendored preprocessor
# output, stored in the repo (referenced rather than embedded — it can be hundreds of KB):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel aNGD_check_talk_msg_no
    stwu    r1,-16(r1)
    mflr    r0
    stw     r0,20(r1)
    stw     r31,12(r1)
    mr      r31,r3
    li      r3,8
    mr      r4,r31
    bl       mDemo_Check
    cmpwi   r3,1
    bne-     .L84
    bl       mMsg_Get_base_window_p
    bl       mMsg_Get_msg_num
    addi    r0,r3,-10953
    cmplwi  r0,10
    bgt-     .L74
    lis     r3,jtbl_376@ha
    slwi    r0,r0,2
    addi    r3,r3,jtbl_376@l
    lwzx    r0,r3,r0
    mtctr   r0
    bctr
.L54:
    li      r3,8
    b        .L78
.L5c:
    li      r3,4
    b        .L78
.L64:
    li      r3,2
    b        .L78
.L6c:
    li      r3,1
    b        .L78
.L74:
    li      r3,0
.L78:
    lwz     r0,2492(r31)
    or      r0,r0,r3
    stw     r0,2492(r31)
.L84:
    lwz     r0,20(r1)
    lwz     r31,12(r1)
    mtlr    r0
    addi    r1,r1,16
    blr
.rodata
glabel jtbl_376
.word .L54
.word .L74
.word .L74
.word .L74
.word .L5c
.word .L74
.word .L64
.word .L74
.word .L74
.word .L74
.word .L6c
ASM_INPUT

# The project context the benchmark passed via --context: the VERBATIM vendored blob — this
# function's translation unit run through the project's own preprocessor without the function, and
# nothing added (where that preprocessor is CodeWarrior's, every other function body is removed too,
# because m2c reads only declarations and cannot parse CodeWarrior's inline asm). How much that is
# varies by project (a full header tree for some, a handful of typedefs for others); the file below
# is the exact bytes, so read it rather than this comment.
# One line is appended: the function's own prototype, and ONLY because the project's headers do
# not declare it and the row's asmlift `--proto` already carries the same void-ness. It is
# derived from that field, never from the reference source.
gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/ctx-deac449e2108.i.gz" > ctx.h
cat >> ctx.h <<'CTX_PROTO'
void aNGD_check_talk_msg_no();
CTX_PROTO

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function aNGD_check_talk_msg_no # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the project context header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `aNGD_check_talk_msg_no` — benchmark function ac-decomp:aNGD_check_talk_msg_no:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# This function's decomp project — the PINNED benchmark branch (provenance base + one
# integration commit). Not needed to run this script (inputs are embedded/vendored); to
# rebuild the project itself:
#   git clone --branch asmlift-benchmark https://github.com/macabeus/ac-decomp.git ac-decomp
#   make -C ac-decomp
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH module foresta's symbol map (the module's own symbols over the
# base ELF's globals — this function lives in a REL module, and its code names the module's
# symbols), vendored at apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/symbols/foresta.json.gz
#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: 1c0cf8cc46e28c086cae896eaa8620594f1cbb9b8a2800118f784919e9f2ec31
# Set PROJECT_PATH to your BUILT checkout of the project above (clone recipe in the comments);
# step 1 then points the scoring config at the checkout's decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.elf) —
# the CLI loads the same map, so this run reproduces the row's named spellings. A missing
# checkout/ELF warns and runs map-less (output may then differ from the row).
# Step 3 passes --module foresta: the CLI then reads that module's ELF, which the build writes
# beside the one decomp.yaml names, and places its sections instead of collapsing them onto 0x0.
PROJECT_PATH='/path/to/ac-decomp'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# the flags of this function's unit, copied from the project's build.
# --project-root grafts the checkout's tools.asmlift.elf (the symbol map) into that decomp.yaml.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target ac-decomp:aNGD_check_talk_msg_no:mwcc_242_81 --out "$PWD" --project-root "$PROJECT_PATH" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────

cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `aPMAN_set_move_idx` — benchmark function ac-decomp:aPMAN_set_move_idx:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'
# asmlift checkout — this function's context is the project's own vendored preprocessor
# output, stored in the repo (referenced rather than embedded — it can be hundreds of KB):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel aPMAN_set_move_idx
    lbz     r5,2459(r3)
    lis     r4,move_idx$345@ha
    lbz     r0,2461(r3)
    addi    r3,r4,move_idx$345@l
    extsb   r4,r5
    mulli   r4,r4,7
    extsb   r0,r0
    add     r3,r3,r4
    lbzx    r3,r3,r0
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# The project context the benchmark passed via --context: the VERBATIM vendored blob — this
# function's translation unit run through the project's own preprocessor without the function, and
# nothing added (where that preprocessor is CodeWarrior's, every other function body is removed too,
# because m2c reads only declarations and cannot parse CodeWarrior's inline asm). How much that is
# varies by project (a full header tree for some, a handful of typedefs for others); the file below
# is the exact bytes, so read it rather than this comment.
gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/ctx-231cc65a97d0.i.gz" > ctx.h

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function aPMAN_set_move_idx # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the project context header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# This function's decomp project — the PINNED benchmark branch (provenance base + one
# integration commit). Not needed to run this script (inputs are embedded/vendored); to
# rebuild the project itself:
#   git clone --branch asmlift-benchmark https://github.com/macabeus/ac-decomp.git ac-decomp
#   make -C ac-decomp
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH module foresta's symbol map (the module's own symbols over the
# base ELF's globals — this function lives in a REL module, and its code names the module's
# symbols), vendored at apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/symbols/foresta.json.gz
#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: 1c0cf8cc46e28c086cae896eaa8620594f1cbb9b8a2800118f784919e9f2ec31
# Set PROJECT_PATH to your BUILT checkout of the project above (clone recipe in the comments);
# step 1 then points the scoring config at the checkout's decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.elf) —
# the CLI loads the same map, so this run reproduces the row's named spellings. A missing
# checkout/ELF warns and runs map-less (output may then differ from the row).
# Step 3 passes --module foresta: the CLI then reads that module's ELF, which the build writes
# beside the one decomp.yaml names, and places its sections instead of collapsing them onto 0x0.
PROJECT_PATH='/path/to/ac-decomp'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# the flags of this function's unit, copied from the project's build.
# --project-root grafts the checkout's tools.asmlift.elf (the symbol map) into that decomp.yaml.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
# (real tier: candidates are scored INSIDE a project context — step 1 materializes ONE rung of
# the benchmark's escalation ladder next to target.o as ctx.i, and the generated decomp.yaml
# concatenates it ahead of every candidate. That rung is the one THIS ROW'S PUBLISHED SOURCE
# stops at — the richest rung on a row asmlift declined — while the harness escalates PER
# CANDIDATE. So this reproduces the row; it does not reproduce a CHANGED asmlift, whose new
# candidate may name a project type this rung does not declare. See docs/ranked-repro.md,
# "What this vehicle does NOT reproduce".)

  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target mwcc_242_81    # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name aQMgr_decide_idx_prob_table # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --asm-data dump.txt     # the data sections above (jump-table/const recovery)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --context declarations.i # the project declarations above
  --module foresta        # the REL module this function lives in: its ELF is the row's symbol map
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)

# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

scripts.m2c:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `bite_check` — benchmark function ac-decomp:bite_check:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'
# asmlift checkout — this function's context is the project's own vendored preprocessor
# output, stored in the repo (referenced rather than embedded — it can be hundreds of KB):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel bite_check
    lis     r4,aGYO_ctrlActor@ha
    li      r3,0
    addi    r4,r4,aGYO_ctrlActor@l
    li      r5,0
    lwz     r4,0(r4)
    addi    r4,r4,372
    b        .L38
.L1c:
    lhz     r0,576(r4)
    rlwinm. r0,r0,0,30,30
    beq-     .L30
    li      r3,1
    blr
.L30:
    addi    r4,r4,592
    addi    r5,r5,1
.L38:
    extsh   r0,r5
    cmpwi   r0,2
    blt+     .L1c
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# The project context the benchmark passed via --context: the VERBATIM vendored blob — this
# function's translation unit run through the project's own preprocessor without the function, and
# nothing added (where that preprocessor is CodeWarrior's, every other function body is removed too,
# because m2c reads only declarations and cannot parse CodeWarrior's inline asm). How much that is
# varies by project (a full header tree for some, a handful of typedefs for others); the file below
# is the exact bytes, so read it rather than this comment.
gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/ctx-279bf430fc5e.i.gz" > ctx.h

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function bite_check   # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the project context header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s
scripts.asmlift:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `bite_check` — benchmark function ac-decomp:bite_check:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# This function's decomp project — the PINNED benchmark branch (provenance base + one
# integration commit). Not needed to run this script (inputs are embedded/vendored); to
# rebuild the project itself:
#   git clone --branch asmlift-benchmark https://github.com/macabeus/ac-decomp.git ac-decomp
#   make -C ac-decomp
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH module foresta's symbol map (the module's own symbols over the
# base ELF's globals — this function lives in a REL module, and its code names the module's
# symbols), vendored at apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/symbols/foresta.json.gz
#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: 1c0cf8cc46e28c086cae896eaa8620594f1cbb9b8a2800118f784919e9f2ec31
# Set PROJECT_PATH to your BUILT checkout of the project above (clone recipe in the comments);
# step 1 then points the scoring config at the checkout's decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.elf) —
# the CLI loads the same map, so this run reproduces the row's named spellings. A missing
# checkout/ELF warns and runs map-less (output may then differ from the row).
# Step 3 passes --module foresta: the CLI then reads that module's ELF, which the build writes
# beside the one decomp.yaml names, and places its sections instead of collapsing them onto 0x0.
PROJECT_PATH='/path/to/ac-decomp'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# the flags of this function's unit, copied from the project's build.
# --project-root grafts the checkout's tools.asmlift.elf (the symbol map) into that decomp.yaml.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target ac-decomp:bite_check:mwcc_242_81 --out "$PWD" --project-root "$PROJECT_PATH" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact `objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'

Disassembly of section .text:

  38:	extsh   r0,r5

# the benchmark's escalation ladder next to target.o as ctx.i, and the generated decomp.yaml
# concatenates it ahead of every candidate. That rung is the one THIS ROW'S PUBLISHED SOURCE
# stops at — the richest rung on a row asmlift declined — while the harness escalates PER
# CANDIDATE. So this reproduces the row; it does not reproduce a CHANGED asmlift, whose new
# candidate may name a project type this rung does not declare. See docs/ranked-repro.md,
# "What this vehicle does NOT reproduce".)

  --target mwcc_242_81    # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name bite_check       # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)

)

# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.

# The project declarations the benchmark lifted this row against (asmlift's --context): the row's
# vendored unit context, VERBATIM. What it declares decides spellings, e.g. a member of a struct
# array the project declares is spelled through that array. It is not always the scoring rung
# step 1 writes as ctx.i, which can be smaller.
gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/ctx-bf7fdee9f1bd.i.gz" > declarations.i

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
# (real tier: candidates are scored INSIDE a project context — step 1 materializes ONE rung of
# the benchmark's escalation ladder next to target.o as ctx.i, and the generated decomp.yaml
# concatenates it ahead of every candidate. That rung is the one THIS ROW'S PUBLISHED SOURCE
# stops at — the richest rung on a row asmlift declined — while the harness escalates PER
# CANDIDATE. So this reproduces the row; it does not reproduce a CHANGED asmlift, whose new
# candidate may name a project type this rung does not declare. See docs/ranked-repro.md,
# "What this vehicle does NOT reproduce".)
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target mwcc_242_81    # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name EffectBG_object_before_display_xlu # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --asm-data dump.txt     # the data sections above (jump-table/const recovery)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --context declarations.i # the project declarations above
  --module foresta        # the REL module this function lives in: its ELF is the row's symbol map
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

# The project declarations the benchmark lifted this row against (asmlift's --context): the row's
# vendored unit context, VERBATIM. What it declares decides spellings, e.g. a member of a struct
# array the project declares is spelled through that array. It is not always the scoring rung

gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/ctx-df653424d8e7.i.gz" > declarations.i

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
# (real tier: candidates are scored INSIDE a project context — step 1 materializes ONE rung of
# the benchmark's escalation ladder next to target.o as ctx.i, and the generated decomp.yaml
# concatenates it ahead of every candidate. That rung is the one THIS ROW'S PUBLISHED SOURCE
# stops at — the richest rung on a row asmlift declined — while the harness escalates PER
# CANDIDATE. So this reproduces the row; it does not reproduce a CHANGED asmlift, whose new
# candidate may name a project type this rung does not declare. See docs/ranked-repro.md,
# "What this vehicle does NOT reproduce".)
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target mwcc_242_81    # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name eNight15Moon_GetNowMoonPos # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --asm-data dump.txt     # the data sections above (jump-table/const recovery)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --context declarations.i # the project declarations above
  --module foresta        # the REL module this function lives in: its ELF is the row's symbol map
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `evw_anime_colreg_manual` — benchmark function ac-decomp:evw_anime_colreg_manual:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'
# asmlift checkout — this function's context is the project's own vendored preprocessor
# output, stored in the repo (referenced rather than embedded — it can be hundreds of KB):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel evw_anime_colreg_manual
    stwu    r1,-16(r1)
    mflr    r0
    stw     r0,20(r1)
    lwz     r8,8336(r3)
    lhz     r7,0(r5)
    lwz     r9,4(r5)
    divwu   r0,r8,r7
    lwz     r6,8(r5)
    mullw   r0,r0,r7
    subf    r0,r0,r8
    mulli   r5,r0,5
    slwi    r0,r0,2
    add     r9,r9,r5
    add     r6,r6,r0
    mr      r5,r9
    bl       evw_color_set
    lwz     r0,20(r1)
    mtlr    r0
    addi    r1,r1,16
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# The project context the benchmark passed via --context: the VERBATIM vendored blob — this
# function's translation unit run through the project's own preprocessor without the function, and
# nothing added (where that preprocessor is CodeWarrior's, every other function body is removed too,
# because m2c reads only declarations and cannot parse CodeWarrior's inline asm). How much that is
# varies by project (a full header tree for some, a handful of typedefs for others); the file below
# is the exact bytes, so read it rather than this comment.
# One line is appended: the function's own prototype, and ONLY because the project's headers do
# not declare it and the row's asmlift `--proto` already carries the same void-ness. It is
# derived from that field, never from the reference source.
gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/ctx-62308bf9be5a.i.gz" > ctx.h
cat >> ctx.h <<'CTX_PROTO'
void evw_anime_colreg_manual();
CTX_PROTO

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function evw_anime_colreg_manual # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the project context header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `evw_anime_colreg_manual` — benchmark function ac-decomp:evw_anime_colreg_manual:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# This function's decomp project — the PINNED benchmark branch (provenance base + one
# integration commit). Not needed to run this script (inputs are embedded/vendored); to
# rebuild the project itself:
#   git clone --branch asmlift-benchmark https://github.com/macabeus/ac-decomp.git ac-decomp
#   make -C ac-decomp
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH module foresta's symbol map (the module's own symbols over the
# base ELF's globals — this function lives in a REL module, and its code names the module's
# symbols), vendored at apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/symbols/foresta.json.gz
#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: 1c0cf8cc46e28c086cae896eaa8620594f1cbb9b8a2800118f784919e9f2ec31
# Set PROJECT_PATH to your BUILT checkout of the project above (clone recipe in the comments);
# step 1 then points the scoring config at the checkout's decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.elf) —
# the CLI loads the same map, so this run reproduces the row's named spellings. A missing
# checkout/ELF warns and runs map-less (output may then differ from the row).
# Step 3 passes --module foresta: the CLI then reads that module's ELF, which the build writes
# beside the one decomp.yaml names, and places its sections instead of collapsing them onto 0x0.
PROJECT_PATH='/path/to/ac-decomp'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# the flags of this function's unit, copied from the project's build.
# --project-root grafts the checkout's tools.asmlift.elf (the symbol map) into that decomp.yaml.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target ac-decomp:evw_anime_colreg_manual:mwcc_242_81 --out "$PWD" --project-root "$PROJECT_PATH" 1>&2

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `lbRTC_RTCTimeToTicks` — benchmark function ac-decomp:lbRTC_RTCTimeToTicks:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# This function's decomp project — the PINNED benchmark branch (provenance base + one
# integration commit). Not needed to run this script (inputs are embedded/vendored); to
# rebuild the project itself:
#   git clone --branch asmlift-benchmark https://github.com/macabeus/ac-decomp.git ac-decomp
#   make -C ac-decomp
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH module foresta's symbol map (the module's own symbols over the
# base ELF's globals — this function lives in a REL module, and its code names the module's
# symbols), vendored at apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/symbols/foresta.json.gz
#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: 1c0cf8cc46e28c086cae896eaa8620594f1cbb9b8a2800118f784919e9f2ec31
# Set PROJECT_PATH to your BUILT checkout of the project above (clone recipe in the comments);
# step 1 then points the scoring config at the checkout's decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.elf) —
# the CLI loads the same map, so this run reproduces the row's named spellings. A missing
# checkout/ELF warns and runs map-less (output may then differ from the row).
# Step 3 passes --module foresta: the CLI then reads that module's ELF, which the build writes
# beside the one decomp.yaml names, and places its sections instead of collapsing them onto 0x0.
PROJECT_PATH='/path/to/ac-decomp'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# the flags of this function's unit, copied from the project's build.
# --project-root grafts the checkout's tools.asmlift.elf (the symbol map) into that decomp.yaml.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target ac-decomp:lbRTC_RTCTimeToTicks:mwcc_242_81 --out "$PWD" --project-root "$PROJECT_PATH" 1>&2

# vendored unit context, VERBATIM. What it declares decides spellings, e.g. a member of a struct
# array the project declares is spelled through that array. It is not always the scoring rung
# step 1 writes as ctx.i, which can be smaller.
gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/ctx-e673c9c56e02.i.gz" > declarations.i

# ── Step 3: decompile + benchmark-grade scoring ──────────────────────────────
# (real tier: candidates are scored INSIDE a project context — step 1 materializes ONE rung of
# the benchmark's escalation ladder next to target.o as ctx.i, and the generated decomp.yaml
# concatenates it ahead of every candidate. That rung is the one THIS ROW'S PUBLISHED SOURCE
# stops at — the richest rung on a row asmlift declined — while the harness escalates PER
# CANDIDATE. So this reproduces the row; it does not reproduce a CHANGED asmlift, whose new
# candidate may name a project type this rung does not declare. See docs/ranked-repro.md,
# "What this vehicle does NOT reproduce".)
args=(
  in.asm                  # input: the disassembly text above
  --target mwcc_242_81    # frontend + target description (ISA, calling convention, compiler idioms)
  --name lbRTC_RTCTimeToTicks # the symbol to decompile (multi-function input selects by name)
  --asm-data dump.txt     # the data sections above (jump-table/const recovery)
  --proto proto.json      # the prototype hints above (callee arities / void-ness)
  --config decomp.yaml    # the compile command from step 1
  --context declarations.i # the project declarations above
  --module foresta        # the REL module this function lives in: its ELF is the row's symbol map
  --score-against target.o # rank the candidates, objdiff-score each; exit 0 only on byte-exact
)
# the checkout's own asmlift bin — the BUILT bundle, not the repo's TypeScript sources run
# through a loader. That build output is gitignored, so a fresh clone's first `pnpm install`
# cannot create this link (it warns `Failed to create bin … ENOENT` and skips it): run
# `pnpm --filter @asmlift/cli build` in the checkout, then `pnpm install` again.
"$ASMLIFT_PATH/node_modules/.bin/asmlift" "${args[@]}"

# Reproduce asmlift on `mEv_clear_status` — benchmark function ac-decomp:mEv_clear_status:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# This function's decomp project — the PINNED benchmark branch (provenance base + one
# integration commit). Not needed to run this script (inputs are embedded/vendored); to
# rebuild the project itself:
#   git clone --branch asmlift-benchmark https://github.com/macabeus/ac-decomp.git ac-decomp
#   make -C ac-decomp
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH module foresta's symbol map (the module's own symbols over the
# base ELF's globals — this function lives in a REL module, and its code names the module's
# symbols), vendored at apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/symbols/foresta.json.gz
#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: 1c0cf8cc46e28c086cae896eaa8620594f1cbb9b8a2800118f784919e9f2ec31
# Set PROJECT_PATH to your BUILT checkout of the project above (clone recipe in the comments);
# step 1 then points the scoring config at the checkout's decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.elf) —
# the CLI loads the same map, so this run reproduces the row's named spellings. A missing
# checkout/ELF warns and runs map-less (output may then differ from the row).
# Step 3 passes --module foresta: the CLI then reads that module's ELF, which the build writes
# beside the one decomp.yaml names, and places its sections instead of collapsing them onto 0x0.
PROJECT_PATH='/path/to/ac-decomp'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# the flags of this function's unit, copied from the project's build.
# --project-root grafts the checkout's tools.asmlift.elf (the symbol map) into that decomp.yaml.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target ac-decomp:mEv_clear_status:mwcc_242_81 --out "$PWD" --project-root "$PROJECT_PATH" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────

cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'

scripts.m2c:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `mFI_BGDisplayListTop` — benchmark function ac-decomp:mFI_BGDisplayListTop:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'
# asmlift checkout — this function's context is the project's own vendored preprocessor
# output, stored in the repo (referenced rather than embedded — it can be hundreds of KB):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel mFI_BGDisplayListTop
    lis     r3,g_fdinfo@ha
    addi    r3,r3,g_fdinfo@l
    lwz     r3,0(r3)
    addi    r3,r3,8
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# The project context the benchmark passed via --context: the VERBATIM vendored blob — this
# function's translation unit run through the project's own preprocessor without the function, and
# nothing added (where that preprocessor is CodeWarrior's, every other function body is removed too,
# because m2c reads only declarations and cannot parse CodeWarrior's inline asm). How much that is
# varies by project (a full header tree for some, a handful of typedefs for others); the file below
# is the exact bytes, so read it rather than this comment.
gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/ctx-d4269c290d0a.i.gz" > ctx.h

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function mFI_BGDisplayListTop # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the project context header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

scripts.m2c:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce m2c on `setScissorView` — benchmark function ac-decomp:setScissorView:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# m2c checkout (https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c); the benchmark pins commit 708d2d2:
#   git clone https://github.com/matt-kempster/m2c && git -C m2c checkout 708d2d2cb2698f091a92492b328f73b24209f72d
M2C_PATH='/path/to/m2c'
# asmlift checkout — this function's context is the project's own vendored preprocessor
# output, stored in the repo (referenced rather than embedded — it can be hundreds of KB):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# The benchmark's objdump→GNU-as normalization of this function's disassembly (m2c cannot
# read raw objdump), including the jump-table/const data sections recovered from the target
# object — the exact text the benchmark fed m2c.
cat > in.s <<'ASM_INPUT'
glabel setScissorView
    lwz     r5,0(r4)
    lwz     r0,4(r4)
    stw     r5,4(r3)
    stw     r0,8(r3)
    lwz     r5,8(r4)
    lwz     r0,12(r4)
    stw     r5,12(r3)
    stw     r0,16(r3)
    lwz     r0,280(r3)
    ori     r0,r0,2
    stw     r0,280(r3)
    blr
ASM_INPUT

# The project context the benchmark passed via --context: the VERBATIM vendored blob — this
# function's translation unit run through the project's own preprocessor without the function, and
# nothing added (where that preprocessor is CodeWarrior's, every other function body is removed too,
# because m2c reads only declarations and cannot parse CodeWarrior's inline asm). How much that is
# varies by project (a full header tree for some, a handful of typedefs for others); the file below
# is the exact bytes, so read it rather than this comment.
gunzip -kc "$ASMLIFT_PATH/apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/ctx-acbbfae0e7ae.i.gz" > ctx.h

args=(
  --target ppc-mwcc-c     # ISA + compiler dialect (selects m2c's code-shape assumptions)
  --function setScissorView # the symbol to decompile from in.s
  --context ctx.h         # the project context header written above
  --no-cache              # bypass m2c's on-disk cache — always a fresh run
)
python3 "$M2C_PATH/m2c.py" "${args[@]}" in.s

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduce asmlift on `setScissorView` — benchmark function ac-decomp:setScissorView:mwcc_242_81.
set -euo pipefail

# asmlift checkout — run `pnpm install` there once, with this function's toolchain available
# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# This function's decomp project — the PINNED benchmark branch (provenance base + one
# integration commit). Not needed to run this script (inputs are embedded/vendored); to
# rebuild the project itself:
#   git clone --branch asmlift-benchmark https://github.com/macabeus/ac-decomp.git ac-decomp
#   make -C ac-decomp
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH module foresta's symbol map (the module's own symbols over the
# base ELF's globals — this function lives in a REL module, and its code names the module's
# symbols), vendored at apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/symbols/foresta.json.gz
#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: 1c0cf8cc46e28c086cae896eaa8620594f1cbb9b8a2800118f784919e9f2ec31
# Set PROJECT_PATH to your BUILT checkout of the project above (clone recipe in the comments);
# step 1 then points the scoring config at the checkout's decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.elf) —
# the CLI loads the same map, so this run reproduces the row's named spellings. A missing
# checkout/ELF warns and runs map-less (output may then differ from the row).
# Step 3 passes --module foresta: the CLI then reads that module's ELF, which the build writes
# beside the one decomp.yaml names, and places its sections instead of collapsing them onto 0x0.
PROJECT_PATH='/path/to/ac-decomp'

# ── Step 1: scoring inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Builds this function's target object (content-cached) and writes a decomp.yaml whose compile
# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
# command carries the flags the target and every candidate compile with, and step 1 prints them:
# the flags of this function's unit, copied from the project's build.
# --project-root grafts the checkout's tools.asmlift.elf (the symbol map) into that decomp.yaml.
# (progress goes to stderr so the script's stdout stays purely the decompiled source)
pnpm --dir "$ASMLIFT_PATH" bench target ac-decomp:setScissorView:mwcc_242_81 --out "$PWD" --project-root "$PROJECT_PATH" 1>&2

# ── Step 2: the input the benchmark fed asmlift, verbatim ────────────────────
# The exact `objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn` text.
cat > in.asm <<'ASM_INPUT'

# (`pnpm bench setup` fetches bench-owned toolchains + pinned project checkouts;
# apps/benchmark/README lists the env-var overrides; .github/workflows/benchmark.yml shows a
# complete from-scratch setup):
ASMLIFT_PATH='/path/to/asmlift'

# This function's decomp project — the PINNED benchmark branch (provenance base + one
# integration commit). Not needed to run this script (inputs are embedded/vendored); to
# rebuild the project itself:
#   git clone --branch asmlift-benchmark https://github.com/macabeus/ac-decomp.git ac-decomp
#   make -C ac-decomp
# SYMBOLS: this row ran WITH the project's symbol map (names + declaration shapes derived
# from the ELF its decomp.yaml names), vendored at apps/benchmark/dataset/real/tu/ac-decomp/symbols.json.gz
#   sha256 of the decompressed map JSON: c77d287cfabc8ae3b46a1bf9cd7a8d90de1abba12a4a2b5c6f20136abce725c3
# Set PROJECT_PATH to your BUILT checkout of the project above (clone recipe in the comments);
# step 1 then points the scoring config at the checkout's decomp.yaml (tools.asmlift.elf) —
# the CLI loads the same map, so this run reproduces the row's named spellings. A missing
# checkout/ELF warns and runs map-less (output may then differ from the row).
PROJECT_PATH='/path/to/ac-decomp'

# command is the benchmark's own toolchain invocation — what --score-against compiles with. That
